title: Tempo Courier — edge routing & VPC onramp scratchpad
content:
Meeting: Tempo Courier kickoff (edge routing + private control plane)
Date: 2025-11-03 10:00 PT (60m) — capture of my notes + quick decisions / open questions.
Attendees: Tom (Tempo eng), Aisha (Tempo infra), Zoe (product), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE)
Purpose: capture Tempo's immediate success criteria for pilot, constraints for private deployment, and a prioritized list of integration tasks.

--- Summary / success criteria (as understood)
- Primary goal: route pick-up/delivery assistant requests from Tempo mobile app to a low-latency inference endpoint (<60ms p50 ideally; p95 <150ms) for short chat-style generation and reranking.
- Security: customer requires VPC peering + private control plane, KMS-managed keys for logs and any cached payloads, and retention policy of logs = 30 days.
- Throughput: expected baseline 120 QPS, burst to 400 QPS during dispatch surges. Average prompt length small (<=100 tokens), rerank calls smaller (~5–20 tokens).
- Cost target: keep per-request marginal cost under $0.006 at baseline using batching/quantization.

--- Architecture notes (sketch, not a diagram)
- Tempo mobile -> regional API gateway (Tempo) -> VPC peering -> Redwood Private control plane endpoints in us-west-2.
- Serving: prefer dedicated pool with a mix of a quantized 8-bit variant for generation and a smaller FP16 variant for reranking/few-shot tasks.
- Caching: enable prefix caching for repeated static prompts (fare-estimates, standard replies). Use per-customer KV cache namespace.
- Smart routing policy: route to lower-cost quantized model when latency budget allows; fallback to FP16 during tail-latency spikes.

--- Immediate technical constraints / gotchas called out by Tempo
- Tempo infra is mostly EKS in their account; their security team is strict about inbound rules — only whitelisted IP ranges or VPC peering allowed. No public endpoint by default.
- Auditing: they need S3 audit exports to their account; Redwood must support cross-account delivery (signed role).
- Tokenization mismatch: Tempo uses their own prompt preprocessor that appends short metadata; need to validate our tokenizer and token counts, especially with whitespace-heavy metadata.
- Mobile SDK wants streaming responses; careful with our chosen quantized model + streaming (some runtimes buffer). We suggested streaming shim but flagged as implementation risk.

--- Performance assumptions (to validate in pilot)
- Batch size defaults: start with continuous batching target of 8 for generation to hit cost target without exceeding p95.
- KV cache hit rate target: 25% for common system prompts; if lower, we may not hit cost goals.
- Network RTT from Tempo mobile -> us-west region: measure with synthetic from their infra and sample device telemetry.

--- Action items / next steps (owner, ETA)
- TEMPO-1: Tempo to provide representative 48h traffic trace (anonymized) + sample prompts (Aisha) — due 2025-11-07.
- TEMPO-2: Redwood (Ethan/Priya) to spin up a dev-private control plane in a sandbox (us-west-2) and expose test VPC peering instructions — due 2025-11-10.
- TEMPO-3: Redwood to run tokenizer parity test and report tokenization diffs for sample prompts (Liam) — due 2025-11-06.
- TEMPO-4: Add backlog ticket for streaming shim performance test for quantized model (internal perf team) — JIRA-TEMPO-112 assigned to Priya (2025-11-12).
- TEMPO-5: Security checklist — cross-account S3 export role + KMS key policy draft (Priya + Tempo security) — due 2025-11-09.

--- Risks / open questions
- If prefix caching hit rate is <15%, cost target likely missed. Need to instrument early.
- Streaming + low-precision models: some runtimes break streaming with continuous batching; fallback strategy must be evaluated before can commit to SDK streaming.
- Autoscale during dispatch surge: Dedicated pool sizing must allow for 400 QPS bursts; question of whether burst is short (minutes) or sustained (hours). If sustained, reserved capacity pricing applies.
- Data residency/regulatory: Tempo asked about EU residency for later expansion — note to pre-check Redwood region availability in eu-west-1.

--- Notes from the call (raw / shorthand)
- Tom: "can't tolerate bad hallucinations on address parsing" — implies need for post-filter or deterministic reranker + allowlist.
- Zoe: wants A/B test for quantized vs FP16 on a 1% user subset. We proposed canary route by token: route X% traffic to model variant.
- Aisha: asked about push logs -> their SIEM (Splunk); we said support via cross-account S3 then ingestion pipeline on their side.

--- Quick config suggestions to include in pilot plan (will convert to infra tickets)
- Model profile: generation: model-8q8a (quant-8) with fallback model-fp16-gen; reranking: model-rank-small-fp16.
- Batching: target continuous_batch_size=8, max_batch_latency_ms=20. Tunable after synthetic tests.
- Caching: enable prefix_cache=true, per_customer_namespace=tempo-alpha. TTL=300s for ephemeral responses, 30d for debug logs only.
- Observability: enable token-latency broken down by model variant, per-route p50/p95, and per-token cost. Export telemetry to Tempo via cross-account S3 + webhook for critical alerts.

--- Deliverables for next meeting (2025-11-12)
- Redwood: sandbox VPC peering guide + initial private control plane endpoint + tokenizer parity report.
- Tempo: cleaned sample prompts + traffic profile + security contact for S3 role.

--- Random thoughts / follow-ups to myself
- Look into streaming shim implementation notes from eng/serving-runtime — link to PRs in call notes later.
- Remind product to confirm pricing model for short bursts vs sustained commit.
- Schedule 30m perf sync with perf eng and Tempo after we ingest the trace.

-- end of scratchpad --
